body:
FINDING (verified). The README's own quickstart ("Quickstart — the CLI", README.md:60-70) tells a newcomer to run `loam register plant.json --home ./my-store` but never ships `plant.json` — the reader must first author a full registration object by hand, including a raw rhizomatic gather Term (the five-level nested `group`/`select`/`mask` shape documented later under "Schemas are data", README.md:118-150+). There is no `--stock` flag or equivalent on `loam register` today (`grep -n "stock" src/cli/cli.ts README.md` — zero matches), and no shipped schema library in the package itself — the closest precedent is `demos/village/schemas/*.json` (person.json, film.json, etc.), which are demo fixtures, not a package-shipped, documented library. So the very first thing a newcomer needs — store a note — requires understanding gather Terms, pointer contexts, and Policy folds before writing a single fact, which is a steep floor for "day one."

FIX SHAPE: (1) a small library of stock registrations shipped IN the package (e.g. `src/stock/` or `demos`-adjacent, exported as data — JSON or TS objects — for `note`, `person`, `event`, `post` at minimum, each a complete `{ hyperschema, schema, roots?, writable?, mutations? }` registration using the plain-entity gather idiom). (2) `loam register --stock <name>` on the CLI: skip the positional file argument, look up the named stock registration, and register it exactly as `loam register <file>` would (reuse `cmdRegister`'s registration path, don't duplicate it). List available stock names in `--help`/on a bad name. (3) README quickstart updated to `loam register --stock note --home ./my-store` as the friction-free path, with the hand-authored-Term walkthrough kept as the deeper "Schemas are data" explanation for when a reader outgrows the stock set.

RAILS: a CLI test in test/cli/cli.test.ts registering `--stock note` (or each stock name) against a fresh home, then serving/querying through it to confirm the registered schema actually resolves a written fact; a test asserting an unknown `--stock` name errors with the available list rather than a raw file-not-found message.

CARE: this ADDS surface (a new flag, a new shipped data library, a new registration path) rather than repairing stated behavior — Myk merges (P6), not self-merge.
title: `loam register --stock <name>` — a shipped library of stock schemas so day one doesn't require hand-authoring a rhizomatic gather Term
